memory_verse.label: Bible Reference
memory_verse.text: Sihon king of the Amorites, who reigned in Heshbon. He ruled from Aroer on the rim of the Arnon Gorge—from the middle of the gorge—to the Jabbok River, which is the border of the Ammonites. This included half of Gilead. He also ruled over the eastern Arabah from the Sea of Galilee to the Sea of the Arabah, and also from Beth Jeshimoth southward below the slopes of Pisgah - Josh 12:2-3 (NIV)

devotion.label: Devotion
devotion.text:
The first king on the list is Sihon, and his defeat did not happen under Joshua at all — it happened years earlier, under Moses, before Israel had even crossed the Jordan (Num 21). The writer reaches back and includes these older victories in the record. The story of God's faithfulness did not begin with Joshua; it stretched back through Moses and further still.

There is something reassuring in that long view. God's work in your life did not start the day you first noticed it. Before you were aware, He was already at work — arranging, protecting, preparing the ground. The victory over Sihon was won by a previous leader, yet it still counted as part of the inheritance Israel now enjoyed.

We stand on ground others fought for before us. The faith we hold was carried to us by people who battled and prayed and believed in generations we never met. Paul reminded Timothy of the faith that lived first in his grandmother and mother (2 Tim 1:5). None of us begins from nothing; we inherit the fruit of God's long faithfulness through those who went ahead. And behind every human link stands the God who has been working out His redemptive plan since before the world began (Eph 1:4).

reflection.label: Reflection
reflection.text:
- Who fought the battles of faith that you now benefit from?
- How does it humble you to know God was working before you noticed?
- For whom might you be winning ground that a future generation will inherit?

prayer.label: Prayer
prayer.text: Father, thank You that Your faithfulness reaches back long before I was aware of it. Help me to honour those who went before me and to serve those who come after. Amen.
